name: MMTweets
description: Finding previously debunked narratives involves identifying claims that have already undergone fact-checking. The issue intensifies when similar false claims persist in multiple languages, despite the availability of debunks for several months in another language. Hence, automatically finding debunks (or fact-checks) in multiple languages is crucial to make the best use of scarce fact-checkers' resources. Mainly due to the lack of readily available data, this is an understudied problem, particularly when considering the cross-lingual scenario, i.e. the retrieval of debunks in a language different from the language of the online post being checked. This study introduces cross-lingual debunked narrative retrieval and addresses this research gap by: (i) creating Multilingual Misinformation Tweets (MMTweets): a dataset that stands out, featuring cross-lingual pairs, images, human annotations, and fine-grained labels, making it a comprehensive resource compared to its counterparts; (ii) con
reputation: A specialized multilingual misinformation retrieval dataset that is useful for cross-lingual fact-checking research but not yet broadly adopted as a standard benchmark.
notes: Cross-lingual retrieval over misinformation/debunk pairs with images and human annotations; relatively small and task-specific, with likely limited leaderboard saturation.
